text:
evan: heads-up — EU region hit sustained GPU contention during the 11:00 window. a few customer L7s observed model substitutions to smaller variants and a latency bump. thinking about a 'soft SLA detour' flow that intentionally routes certain low-sensitivity requests to non-resident regions with a downgrade policy. thoughts? :thinking:
maria: can you paste the error/trace we saw? curious if it's just autoscaler lag or hot-tenant noise.
evan: logs attached here (excerpt):
```
2026-03-18T11:02:14Z region=eu-west request_id=abc123 serve_pool=dedicated-gpu-1 err=queue-timeout
2026-03-18T11:02:16Z route=eu-primary fallback=eu-lite model=rwkv-7b-lite replaced_by=rwkv-1b
```
```
kevin: autoscaler looked healthy but we had a burst of prep requests from a few customers. autoscaler window is 60s + cooldown; by design it's slow to avoid oscillation.
sophia: i like the idea of an explicit detour policy instead of implicit fallback. two quick constraints: (1) legal/data residency — we must not detour PII-tagged requests; (2) quality — customers on higher tiers should never see silent model downgrades without a flag.
evan: agreed. proposal sketch:
- classify incoming request by residency_flag (resident/nonresident) and sensitivity (pii_low/pii_high)
- three detour modes: 
  1) permissive-detour: send nonresident & pii_low to closest non-eu region with model downgrade allowed
  2) conservative-detour: only nonresident & cached prefix eligible (no model swap)
  3) no-detour: default for pii_high or enterprise-slo routes
- routing priority: local-hosted -> permissive-detour -> conservative -> reject (503)

maria: do we have infra hooks to mark requests as "pii_high" in the proxy? we currently only surface residency tags.
kevin: proxy can inject request-annotations now via header X-Redwood-Flags. we can add X-Redwood-Sensitivity: low|high easily. will need a cross-team opt-in for SDKs.
sophia: also need a transparent tenant-level control: tenant config should be able to opt out of detours, or set allowed downgrades. example config yaml:```yaml
tenant: acme-corp
residency: eu
detour:
  enabled: true
  mode: permissive-detour
  allowed_model_downgrades:
    - rwkv-7b -> rwkv-1b
    - llama-2-13b -> llama-2-7b
  pii_policy: block
```
kevin: quick thought on safety: we should synthesize a header X-Detour-Reason with reason codes so downstream services and logs can filter (e.g., detour=capacity, detour=cost-surge).
evan: ops/console needs to show token-level cost delta and quality telemetry for detoured requests. if a tenant sees quality regressions we must roll policy back.
sophia: rollout plan idea: start as an opt-in feature for a handful of non-regulated tenants. run A/B with quality evals (prompt-suite). if metrics stable, flip to opt-out for small tier customers.
maria: one more operational caveat — KV cache locality. detouring to nonresident region will cause cold KV caches and may spike cost. consider a 'cache-prefetch' prewarm when detour is chosen for a tenant: schedule a background warmup of common prefixes.
kevin: config sample for proxy routing (pseudo):
```
route:
  detour_enabled: true
  detour_policy: permissive-detour
  sensitivity_header: X-Redwood-Sensitivity
  detour_target_order:
    - us-west-2
    - ap-southeast-1
```

sophia: legal check: need a short memo for privacy/legal describing when detour is allowed (only pii_low, nonresident, logged/hashed customer ids, data-retention unaffected). i'll draft.
evan: can deploy-bot run a quick canary on staging to simulate detour behavior? wanna see metrics for 5% traffic.
deploy-bot: canary started: namespace=staging-detour, traffic=5%, models swapped per policy=enabled. will post metrics in 15m. :robot_face:
maria: small UX ask — console should show a per-tenant 'detour history' timeline with counts and reasons, and a toggle to disable. helps support teams.
kevin: popup question: how do we handle in-flight requests if a region is evicting capacity? do we attempt detour mid-request or only at admission time?
evan: prefer admission-time only. mid-request model swap invites correctness bugs with KV cache and attention state. mark as 'admission-only'.
sophia: agree. also add a fallback ladder: if permissive-detour target also saturated, we try next region. stop after N hops (N=3).
maria: tagging for RFC: can someone add an RFC follow-up section 'soft-detour-protocol' with interface definitions (headers, tenant-config, metrics)? i'll volunteer to co-author.
kevIN: +1 — i'll add proxy-level code pointers. (typo in name intentionally showing a quick followup) :thumbsup:
evan: thanks. i'll create the RFC follow-up draft and link to this thread. for now i'll open a Jira for the legal memo and a spike to measure KV prewarm cost.
sophia: sounds good. action items: evan — draft RFC follow-up, kevin — prototype header plumbing, maria — console wireframe, sophia — legal memo, deploy-bot — post canary metrics.
deploy-bot: canary metrics (partial):
- 15m window: 5% traffic -> detours=197, avg-latency+20ms, model-downgrades=48, kb-cache-miss-rate +12%
- health: eu-hosting pool back to 75% after cooldown

evan: nice. let's reconvene after we have full 1h canary results. tagging @maria @kevin @sophia for next steps. :calendar:
